title: SLO Sprint Hive — Cross-functional Reliability Playbook (90d)
summary: Operable, cross-team runbook for operationalizing service-level objectives (SLOs) across model serving, embeddings, and routing. Designed as a 90-day 'Sprint Hive' made of micro-sprints (2-week cycles) to deliver measurable SLO coverage, telemetry maturity, and runbook automation with clear ownership and rollback policies.
objectives: 1) Define and publish SLOs for three priority domains: generation API (hosted), embeddings pipeline, and routing/fallbacks. 2) Implement telemetry coverage and baseline error budgets. 3) Run two controlled rollouts (canary -> progressive) with automated rollback on budget burn. 4) Establish cross-team cadence and handoffs for long-term SLO stewardship.
success_metrics: - Published SLO docs for 3 domains (public). - Telemetry signal coverage >= 90% for SLO alerts (latency, errors, availability). - Two canary rollouts completed with automated rollback configured. - Error budget policy agreed and integrated into paging and runbooks. - Reduction in unplanned sev2/3 incidents related to model serving by 30% vs prior 90 days.
scope-in-scope-out: In-scope: generation API (hosted), embeddings training->serving pipeline, smart routing/fallback logic, telemetry dashboards, alert rules, runbooks, and team training. Out-of-scope: infra migration, billing model changes, customer-level SLA contracts (these are downstream artifacts).
stakeholders_and_roles: Product-hosted-api: Priya Singh (PM) — prioritization and UX; Serving-runtime: Evan Brooks — implementation, kernels and batching hooks; Platform-engineering: Marta Kowalski — deployment gates and capacity; SRE: Lena Park (lead) — SLO design, runbooks, oncall integration; Developer Experience: Ravi Menon — docs, SDK examples; Solutions Eng / CS: Samir Gupta — customer impact and rollout comms.
raci: Responsible: SRE + Serving-runtime engineers. Accountable: SRE lead (Lena Park). Consulted: Product, Platform, DevEx, CS. Informed: Engineering managers, Sales ops for major customer-impacting rollouts.
cadence_and_meetings: Weekly 60m Sprint Hive sync (cross-team): status, blockers, decisions. Twice-weekly micro-sprint check-ins (30m) per domain. Pre-canary readiness review (1h) at -7 days. Canary monitoring war-room (ad-hoc) during rollout. Post-mortem + retro (90m) within 3 business days of any >25% error budget burn.
milestones_and_timeline: Week 0–2: SLO definitions and owners assigned; telemetry gap analysis. Week 3–4: Implement missing metrics and dashboard baselines. Week 5–6: Create runbooks and automated alert playbooks; staging canary test. Week 7–8: Canary rollout for generation API (5% -> 20% -> 50%), monitor error budget. Week 9–10: Retrospective and adjustments; start embeddings micro-SLO experiment. Week 11–12: Progressive rollout for embeddings; finalize routing policies and handoff to SLO stewards. Week 13: Program wrap, publish playbook and handoff schedule.
sample_slos: Generation API availability: 99.95% monthly (measured as successful 2xx responses / total requests, excluding planned maintenance). Error budget: 0.05% of requests per rolling 30d.
Generation latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for requests < 512 tokens, p95 < 600ms for requests 512–2048 tokens (rolling 7d). Alerting: sustained breach for 15m triggers page.
Embeddings pipeline freshness SLO: end-to-end job completion within SLA window (batch daily job finished by 04:00 UTC) 99% of days per 30-day window.
Routing/fallback success SLO: automated fallback to compatible model variant with successful response within 300ms in 99.9% of fallback invocations.
KV cache hit-rate micro-SLO: prefix cache hit-rate >= 75% for high-frequency customers (top 20% by qps) measured over rolling 7d.
telemetry_and_alerting: Minimum telemetry: request count, 2xx/4xx/5xx breakdown, per-model qps, p50/p95/p99 latency by payload-size bucket, kv-cache hit rate, token generation rate, gpu queue length, per-route error budget burn rate. Alerts: error-rate climb >3x baseline for 10m, sustained p95 latency > SLO threshold for 15m, error-budget consumption >50% in 24h. Use tracing spans to attribute latency to kernel, batching, or network.
alert_actions_and_escalation: Tier 1: automated remediation playbooks (scale up burst, enable degraded-mode routing, enable reduced-token-mode). Tier 2: page SLO steward and serving-runtime oncall. Tier 3: full incident bridge and cross-team exec notification if error-budget burnout projected in <12h. Post-incident: update runbook and add regression tests.
rollout_strategy: Canary -> progressive rollout with automated checks. Pre-canary: validate staging load tests and runbook drills. Canary plan for generation API: 5% traffic for 2h, observe telemetry and error budget math; if stable, move to 20% for 4h; then 50% for 12h; then 100% in business off-hours. Each step has automatic rollback if: error rate > SLO threshold AND burn projected to exhaust >25% of budget within 24h, OR sustained latency breaches >2x threshold for 30m.
rollout_checklist: - Owners assigned for canary window. - Baseline dashboards up and annotated. - Automated rollback hooks tested. - Alerting and paging verified. - Communication: customer ops + sales notified. - Post-rollout retro scheduled.
runbook_snippets: On sustained p95 breach: 1) Check model variant routing and kernel fallbacks, 2) Inspect batching metrics and GPU queue length, 3) If GPU queue > 80% and latency rising, temporarily enable burst capacity or reduce per-request token cap, 4) If errors spike, switch canary traffic to fallback variant.
dependencies_and_blockers: - Telemetry infra (metrics ingestion and retention) needs quota increase (Platform ticket). - Automated rollback hook needs a small API change in routing service (Serving-runtime PR). - Legal signoff for public SLO language for embeddings freshness. - Capacity booking for canary windows (Dedicated ops).
budget_and_estimate: Estimated engineering effort: ~4 FTE-weeks distributed across SRE and Serving-runtime for initial sprint; additional 2 FTE-weeks for telemetry infra changes. Operational cost estimate for canary capacity (GPU burst) ~ $8k for the 90-day program. Non-billable ramp: training and runbook rehearsal ~ 3 sessions (1h each).
risk_register: Risk: High burn during canary due to an unexpected model regression. Mitigation: Start small (5%), auto-rollback, and pre-load test models with synthetic adversarial prompts.
Risk: Missing telemetry signals in prod leading to false positives/negatives. Mitigation: dual-read (metric + trace) and synthetic probes for critical paths.
Risk: Cross-team coordination friction leading to missed gates. Mitigation: locked calendar with pre-canary readiness review and exec sponsor who can unblock.
Risk: Customer-facing incidents during rollout harming trust. Mitigation: limit canary to internal quotas or low-traffic regions first; CS notified ahead of time.
Risk: Error budget policy ambiguity. Mitigation: run a tabletop exercise to validate thresholds and paging behavior before rollouts.
open_questions_and_next_steps: - Agree on canonical SLO measurement windows (30d vs 90d) for each domain. - Finalize paging thresholds for embedding freshness failures. - Confirm capacity reservation for canary slots. Next steps: 1) Approve SLO language by 2026-02-16; 2) Complete telemetry gap list by 2026-02-24; 3) Schedule pre-canary readiness review for 2026-03-02.
comms_and_docs_plan: Public-facing SLO page (short, non-legal language) authored by DevEx + Product. Internal playbook (this doc + runbooks) stored in SRE drive and linked from oncall dashboards. One-pager for Sales and CS summarizing impact and mitigation strategy.
postmortem_and-learning: Every incident where error budget consumption >25% triggers a lightweight postmortem (L1) with owners and action items; severe burns (>50%) trigger a full postmortem with exec readout. Capture learnings in a 'SLO Learnings' log and incorporate into onboarding for new stewards.
